actions.name: Threat actors use remote access software for initial access
actions.description: Cyber threat actors use remote access software for initial access, maintaining persistence, deploying additional software and tools, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.

actions.name: Threat actors exploit vulnerable software before leveraging remote access software
actions.description: Before leveraging remote access software as part of an intrusion, cyber actors may exploit vulnerable software including legitimate servers and general network exploitation activities.

actions.name: Threat actors obtain legitimate, compromised remote access software credentials
actions.description: Threat actors may obtain legitimate, compromised remote access software credentials that enable control over remote endpoints associated with the compromised account.

actions.name: Threat actors use PowerShell or similar command line tools to silently deploy RMM agent
actions.description: Once initial access is obtained, threat actors often use PowerShell or similar command line tools to silently deploy the RMM agent.

actions.name: Threat actors leverage multiple RMM mechanisms at once
actions.description: Threat actors leverage multiple RMM mechanisms at once, sometimes in concert with commercial penetration testing tools such as Cobalt Strike or remote access malware to enable multiple, often redundant, forms of access to ensure persistence.

actions.name: Threat actors use remote access software to perform credential dumps and escalate privileges
actions.description: Threat actors use remote access software to perform multiple functions including credential dumps and escalating privileges.

actions.name: Threat actors use PowerShell to silently deploy remote access software
actions.description: Threat actors may use PowerShell to silently deploy remote access software, with industry observations of PowerShell being used to install RMM itself.

actions.name: Threat actors rename NetSupport binary to ctfmon.exe for defense evasion
actions.description: Industry has observed cyber threat actors renaming a NetSupport binary to ctfmon.exe as a defense evasion technique.

actions.name: Threat actors use remote access software to discover remote systems for lateral movement
actions.description: Remote access software may allow threat actors to find lists of other systems on a network that may be used for lateral movement from the current system.

actions.name: Threat actors exploit existing remote services to move laterally
actions.description: Threat actors may exploit existing remote services to move laterally throughout a network.

actions.name: Threat actors exploit valid accounts to log into remote services
actions.description: Threat actors may exploit valid accounts to log into a network or service designed to accept remote connections.

actions.name: Threat actors exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access for lateral movement
actions.description: Threat actors may exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems to move laterally throughout a network.

actions.name: Threat actors establish command and control channels using legitimate remote access software
actions.description: Threat actors may establish command and control channels using legitimate remote access software.

relations.rationale: a1 happens after a2 as stated by 'Before leveraging remote access software as part of an intrusion, cyber actors may exploit vulnerable software.'

a1 depends on a3 because 'Threat actors may also obtain legitimate, compromised remote access software credentials that ultimately enable them to exercise control over remote endpoints associated with the compromised account.'
a4 depends on a1 because 'Once initial access is obtained threat actors often use PowerShell or similar command line tools to silently deploy the RMM agent.'

relations.rationale: a7 depends on a1 because 'Threat actors may use PowerShell to silently deploy remote access software. Industry has observed PowerShell being used to install RMM itself.' This is stated after initial access is obtained.
a5 happens after a1 as stated by 'Often, threat actors leverage multiple RMM mechanisms at once.'
a6 depends on a1 because 'Threat actors use remote access software to perform multiple functions and carry out several commonly associated TTPs (e.g . credential dumps and escalating privileges.)'
relations.epistemic_reason: 引句存在於原文，但沒有陳述先後或相依的字眼；此關係是依敘事順序推論，需人工確認。

relations.rationale: a9 depends on a1 because 'Remote access software may allow threat actors to find lists of other systems on a network that may be used for lateral movement from the current system.'
a10 happens after a9 as stated by 'Threat actors may exploit existing remote services to move laterally throughout a network.'
a11 depends on a10 because 'Threat actors may exploit valid accounts to log into a network or service designed to accept remote connections.'
a12 depends on a10 because 'Threat actors may exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems to move laterally throughout a network.'
a13 depends on a1 because 'Threat actors may establish command and control channels using legitimate remote access software.'
